note: The AmneziaWG obfuscation block of the awg-quick [Interface] section, rendered TWICE in this repository, in two languages, for the two ends of the same tunnel: the node writes the SERVER config (apps/node/internal/core/amneziawg/config.go, renderObfuscation) and the panel writes the CLIENT .conf handed to the buyer (apps/panel-backend/src/core-adapters/amneziawg/wgconf.ts, buildAmneziawgClientConfig). Both read the same pushed values, so the NUMBERS agree by construction; what does not agree by construction is which keys each side emits and how it spells them. The AmneziaWG handshake hashes these parameters in, so a mismatch does not warn, does not log and does not fail a healthcheck — the tunnel simply never decrypts, for every user of that inbound. Measured 2026-08-26: the server side was observed by nothing at all (renaming Jmin, dropping I1-I5 and dropping S3/S4 all passed the whole Go suite in silence) and the client side missed H3. These vectors are the contract: both sides have a test that reads this file.
asymmetry: S3/S4 are the one deliberate difference and the reason this file lists the two sides separately rather than one expected block. The server emits them always; the client omits them when zero, because the AmneziaVPN iOS network extension (checked on 4.8.19) cannot parse those keys at all — even at 0 — and aborts with ParseError 9. Omitting them leaves a 1.x-shaped config every client accepts, and a real 2.0 setup still gets them. Changing this is a product decision about which clients keep working, not a tidy-up.

vectors.name: 2.0: S3/S4 set and three mimicry slots used
